subject: Re: MAP kickoff — POC environment sync & wiring checklist
messages:
From: Erik Morris <erik.morris@carelogic.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: emily.zhao@carelogic.com
Date: 2028-04-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC MAP kickoff — wiring + timeline

Grace — thanks for the intro earlier. Emily and I reviewed the mutual action plan draft and want to align on the exact POC wiring items so our network team can block calendar time. Key asks from our side:

- Org setup: request a sample org invite flow and role matrix so we can map our SREs
- API keys: we need long-lived key generation steps and rotation recommendations (we run weekly rotation)
- IP allowlist: we will provide a short list but need an expected maintenance window for updates
- VPC peering: confirm whether peering is needed for initial eval or only for production (we prefer to test via allowlist first)

Attached is our internal readiness checklist and a rough diagram. Can Redwood provide a single-page action cadence (owner + due date) we can include in the MAP?

Thanks,
Erik
Network & Infra Program Manager
CareLogic

Attachment: carelogic-network-diagram.png (image/png)
Attachment: CL-readiness-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Erik Morris <erik.morris@carelogic.com>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@carelogic.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC MAP kickoff — wiring + timeline

Erik / Emily — great notes. I pulled together a focused 3-week cadence that maps the items you listed into discrete handoffs so your network and security teams can schedule. High level — we propose two phases:

Phase A (Week 1): API keys + org setup + allowlist validation (no VPC peering required)
Phase B (Weeks 2–3): Optional VPC peering + load validation and canary traffic (if you want an isolated path)

I attached a one-pager MAP workbook (MAP-CareLogic-v1.xlsx) with owner columns. Summary of immediate owners below:

- API keys (Grace / Marissa): we will create a scoped test API key for the POC and send a secure link for retrieval. Key type: limited-scope server key, TTL: 30 days by default for the POC. Rotation note: we support weekly rotation — we'll include rotation scripts.
- Org setup (Marissa): we will invite two CareLogic org admins (one SRE, one product) and provide role mappings (admin, developer, auditor).
- IP allowlist (Ben): provide your public egress IPs; we will add them to a temporary allowlist and share maintenance SLA (changes applied within 2 business hours during the POC window).
- VPC peering (Neha): if you opt in, peering requires shared routes and a maintenance window; estimate 5 business days to schedule and validate.

Action items I need from you today to hit Week 1 start on Monday (2028-04-22):
1) Confirm the two org admin contacts (name + email + corporate role)
2) Send a single CSV of public IPs to allowlist (max 25 entries)
3) Confirm whether you want peering scoped now or deferred to Week 2

I'll also add a lightweight acceptance test that verifies token auth, sample generation, and embedding calls. If that looks good I can push the MAP one-pager into HubSpot and tag the HubSpot deal.

On timing — I can host a 30-minute handoff tomorrow at 10:00 PT if your team is available to walk through owners.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: MAP-CareLogic-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@carelogic.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: erik.morris@carelogic.com
Date: 2028-04-17T13:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC MAP kickoff — wiring + timeline

Thanks Grace — the cadence looks good. Quick answers inline:

1) Org admins: 
- Daniel Park (daniel.park@carelogic.com) — SRE lead
- Priya Raman (priya.raman@carelogic.com) — Product infra

2) IP list: attaching small CSV — 3 IPs primarily. We'll keep peering off for now; want to validate via allowlist first.

3) Demo handoff: tomorrow 10:00 PT works for Daniel and me.

We also have a procurement question: what are the minimal IP retention logs we can provide for SOC / audit? Procurement cc'd.

Emily
Senior Product Manager, CareLogic

Attachment: carelogic-iplist.csv (text/csv)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@carelogic.com>, Priya Raman <priya.raman@carelogic.com>, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, emily.zhao@carelogic.com, erik.morris@carelogic.com
Date: 2028-04-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: MAP action items — owners & minimal audit scope

Daniel / Priya — welcome. Per Grace's plan, I am taking point on org invites and the acceptance checklist. Quick notes for your security team:

- Minimal audit logs we can expose for the POC: request logs (timestamp, route, token-id hash, egress IP), and admin audit entries (org invites, role changes). We can provide daily CSV extracts for up to 30 days for the POC.
- API test key delivery: we'll send a DocuSign-like secure retrieval link (one-time view) for the initial key; rotation script included in repo.
- Allowlist changes: Ben will push changes into the allowlist; expected propagation within 2 business hours. If you need emergency unblock outside windows, we have an escalation channel.

Planned deliverables by Friday (2028-04-20):
- Org invites sent (Marissa)
- Test API key delivered and validated (Grace)
- Allowlist applied (Ben)
- Acceptance test run and report (Neha)

If everyone agrees, I'll mark these as MAP sprint items and update the HubSpot deal. Daniel — confirm that CSV you sent contains your true egress addresses and include ASN if possible.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-service-roles.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Erik Morris <erik.morris@carelogic.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: emily.zhao@carelogic.com, daniel.park@carelogic.com, priya.raman@carelogic.com
Date: 2028-04-20T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP action items — owners & minimal audit scope

Team — that looks great and aligned with our security requirements. Quick confirmations:

- We received the org invites and both Daniel and Priya accepted.
- The test API key retrieval link worked for our SRE test harness — validated token auth and sample generation call.
- Allowlist applied; we ran handshake test and connectivity was successful.
- Procurement still wants the daily CSV extracts for logs (to be retained by us for SOC review). Procurement asked for a short attestation on log retention — procurement@carelogic.com is copied.

Next steps:
- Neha, please kick the acceptance test report into the shared Drive folder when ready.
- Marissa, push the MAP one-pager into HubSpot and set the next milestone to "Eval acceptance" on 2028-04-26.

Thanks everyone for the speedy turnaround.

— Erik
Network & Infra Program Manager | CareLogic
